name: Scarisbrick Hall

dates.altered: Successive remodelling of a C16 seat begun in 1814, probably by John Slater of Liverpool and Thomas Rickman; the east wing and tower for Anne Scarisbrick in the 1860s and 1870s by Edward Welby Pugin.
dates.note: The list entry dates A. W. N. Pugin's main campaign 1836-1845. Historic England's own visitor page for the same building says instead that it was 'built between 1830 and 1860', which is a different span from the same body; both are recorded and neither is resolved.

quotes.text: Country house, now school. Successive remodelling, rebuilding and enlargement of C16 seat of the Scarisbrick family, begun in 1814, probably by John Slater (of Liverpool) and Thomas Rickman, but mainly 1836-1845 by Augustus Welby Northmore Pugin for Thomas Scarisbrick, and 1860s and 1870s for Anne Scarisbrick. Sandstone, with stone slate roofs. Hall facing south-east, with east and west crosswings, east tower, kitchens (etc), L-shaped service wing to the rear.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, opening paragraph (List Entry Number 1038565).

quotes.text: All in Gothic style: the west wing of 1814 in early Gothic, the hall and other parts of the main range of 1836-45 in fully developed C15 Gothic revival
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section; the extracted span ends 'the east wing and very high tower in'.

quotes.text: The centre of the composition is Augustus Welby Northmore Pugin's 2-storey open-hall, with 2-storey oriels, steeply pitched roof with 3-stage lantern on the ridge, but it is dominated by Edward Welby Pugin's east wing with an octagonal angle turret surmounted by a cluster of large fluttering birds, and by the tower of extravagant height finished with corner pinnacles and an attenuated rectangular spire.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, second span of the composition paragraph.

quotes.text: The kitchen attached at the east end, by Augustus Welby Northmore Pugin, is likewise in C15 Gothic style, octagonal, with steeply-pitched roof and square lantern.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, kitchen sentence.

note: Tranche 3, British picturesque and Arts and Crafts cluster, 5 Sep 2026. Added as a new exemplar of `gothic-revival-british`. Chosen as a documentary rather than a beautiful case: it is Pugin's largest secular commission, the register describes it as a succession of campaigns whose ornament becomes 'more flamboyant and fanciful in the progression from east to west', and the same body's Heritage at Risk register records it in poor condition -- which is the honest state of a great deal of this style's domestic work and is worth having in the corpus beside the National Trust houses.
